storyline.note: Titles read as an argument: cost → duplication → fit → alternatives → ask. c8's timeline title is a statement of fact, not part of the argument — acceptable for an appendix.

verticalLogic.note: Each card's evidence backs its own title; c5's 92% claim leans on usage logs that are referenced but not shown on the card.

archetypeFit.note: Recommendation on card 2, problem → solution → ask in the prescribed order, appendix excluded from the count.

audienceFit.note: Cost, coverage, deadline and rollback are the right altitude for a budget owner; the seat-duplication chart may invite a tangent on licence hygiene.

density.note: Every card is two blocks or fewer plus a title claim; c6's four-row table is the densest card and still reads in under 30 seconds.

concerns.message: The 92% coverage claim rests on usage-log analysis that is cited but not attached — soften the claim or bring the analysis
No migration-risk card in the main line; the room will ask what breaks during the eight weeks before anyone reaches the appendix
Comparison criteria read as chosen after the decision — adding security-review status would blunt that objection
